conclusion: The shipped v0.12.15 code already handles empty, unknown, wrong-type and unmapped second weapons for locked/unlocked Final, Valor and Master using a form-validated primary Keyblade. Invalid fallback metadata rejects before a native transition. No new product defect was established for this reported case.

sourceAndPackageChecks.scope: Read-only package/source/log verification. No executable, game, attach, process inspection or native test was run by this reviewer. Only this review directory receives output.

behavior.detail: Only forms1/4/5 plan a fallback. A valid existing offhand is retained. Empty/unknown/non-Keyblade/unmapped existing equipment falls back to the main weapon only if it passes the same per-form candidate checks. Unlock bits and inventory quantities are neither required nor granted.

Candidate requires item type2, target object group, bounded went mapping to an available object-table name, and bounded nonempty terminated offhand wmst name. Native skeleton contract is additionally checked in FormSkeletonReady.

Begin rechecks all gates and replans immediately before writing the exact2-byte form equipment slot and invoking NativeBegin. No valid fallback causes safety rejection. No native context rolls back the unconsumed write if unchanged; an existing context retains it for engine use.
An existing form first reverts; target metadata is checked before Revert. DriveTick at395-398 rechecks the fresh base actor and target, then Begin replans from current equipment.

Unknown equipment in the currently active form is rejected by the current-record gate at156 before target repair. This fails closed; the feature does not promise repair of an already-corrupt active form.
Successful fallback is persistent form-slot initialization. It remains after disconnect and can be saved by the game; it is not temporary equipment restoration.

limitations.boundary: ObjectAvailable proves a known object-table row with a bounded nonempty model name; it does not open an archive or ensure every actual model/motion file exists and is loadable.
wmst validation proves a terminated name in a bounded row, not successful asynchronous motion loading.

The test consumer maps every nonzero model to a fabricated valid weapon object. Allocation/asset/parser failure after preflight is untested. It would be incorrect to claim that physically missing/corrupt archive assets cannot still crash the native loader.
After NativeBegin begins asynchronous engine work, no complete constructor/allocator/parser or concurrent-modification guarantee exists. This review includes no in-game confirmation.
